clue.text: Those people 'arkened to scripture a long time ago

parts.note: those people means they
a dropped-aitch spelling of hearkened, as in 'eard for heard, the H gone just as in the clue's own word
OT is the Old Testament, part of scripture

explanation.surface: Folk long ago who listened to scripture, written in dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'arkened is the signal: the H is dropped, so heard becomes 'EARD. THE YEAR DOT is a British idiom for a very long time ago.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the remote past, as in 'since time immemorial'.

clue.text: Name an aid to revolution, possibly

definitions.meaning: a name, or nickname, by which someone is known
a knob or lever you grip to turn something round, such as a door knob or crank

explanation.definitionFit: A moniker is a name; a crank or knob is gripped to turn things.

clue.text: Without a lisp, this juvenile would sound employable

definitions.text: Without a lisp, this juvenile would sound employable

parts.words: Without a lisp, this juvenile would sound employable
parts.note: a lisper says TH for S, so a word meaning juvenile, said as a lisper says it, comes out like a word meaning useful; the clue describes the reverse

explanation.surface: A young job applicant whose speech defect hides how useful they would be.
explanation.walkthrough: Say USEFUL (employable) with a lisp, turning each S into TH, and you get something close to the answer, a word for young.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenile and young-seeming are synonyms.

clue.text: Able to draw — or winning

definitions.meaning: able to pull things towards it, as a magnet pulls iron
winning as in charming, a winning smile

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from drawing in: physically pulling, or being appealing.

clue.text: Steps apparently taken by mysterious men Holmes encountered

definitions.text: Steps apparently taken by mysterious men Holmes encountered

parts.words: Steps apparently taken by mysterious men Holmes encountered
parts.note: the Sherlock Holmes story about stick-figure ciphers drawn like little men in motion; steps here are footwork to music

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes tracking the footsteps of mysterious strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adventure of the Dancing Men is a Sherlock Holmes story in which a code is written as rows of little stick figures that look as if they are moving to music.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking steps to music is moving rhythmically on the floor.

clue.text: Student told to leave Oxford by this sort of drain, initially confused

annotationWithheld.why: Student told to leave Oxford by this sort of drain, initially confused (4): 'drain' is likely an OCR misread of 'train' (a DOWN train; sent down), but no parse gives TOWN from DOWN without inventing a letter change, and no source confirms the clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Student told to leave Oxford by this sort of drain, initially confused

clue.text: Triumphantly flourish health food container

parts.note: bran is the fibre-rich husk eaten as health food
a dish is a container for food

explanation.surface: Proudly waving a bowl of muesli in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave something about in triumph or display.

clue.text: Awfully shy poet entering ambassador's premises

indicators.note: entering says the jumbled letters go inside the ambassador's abbreviation

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador, so ambassador's is HE'S

indicators.note: awfully says the letters of shy poet are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A timid poet arrives at an embassy building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premises' looks like buildings, matching the embassy picture, but it means propositions. HE is His Excellency, the formal title of an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Premises are propositions assumed as a basis for argument, like suppositions.

clue.text: Bird thus returning with kill

indicators.note: returning says the word for thus is read backwards

parts.note: so means thus
a predator's kill is its prey

explanation.surface: A bird coming back with its catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish-eating hawk, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Open up cask, replacing one in students' club

indicators.note: replacing says the cask takes the place of the letter for one

parts.note: a students' union is a students' club
I is the Roman numeral for one
a butt is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: Breaching a barrel at the student bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the I in UNION for BUTT.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo the fastenings of a garment, opening it.

clue.text: Fee paid by stockbroker to study dance

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study
the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A broker paying to take dance lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Contango was a fee paid on the old London Stock Exchange for carrying a deal over to the next settlement day.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge for postponing settlement of a share purchase on the stock exchange.

clue.text: Like Beethoven, finally stringing notes together

definitions.meaning: Beethoven lost his hearing in the last part of his life
four musical note names written one after another spell the word

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: the note names D, E, A and F in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven ended his life unable to hear.

clue.text: Woman's husband served as her kitchen help

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, so woman's is DI'S
served as means was, as in he was captain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A husband doing the washing-up for his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that cleans plates and pans, a help in the kitchen.

clue.text: :Seafood island chef cooked

indicators.note: cooked as in cooked up, so the letters are concocted into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef on an island preparing fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The eulachon, an oily Pacific fish eaten as food.

clue.text: Two pages, one aspiring to catch another insect

parts.note: a leaf of a book is two pages, front and back

indicators.note: to catch says the letter for another page goes inside

parts.note: one who hopes or aspires is a hoper
another page, P being the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Two young servants, one ambitious, trying to catch an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another page, abbreviated P, which 'to catch' puts inside HOPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A small jumping bug that feeds on plant sap.

clue.text: Pony or dog from the isle, originally

definitions.text: Pony or dog from the isle, originally

parts.words: Pony or dog from the isle, originally
parts.note: the name is a pet form used for a breed of sheepdog, and sometimes a pony, that comes from Shetland, Scottish islands

explanation.surface: An animal native to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shetland Isles lie north of Scotland; both the small pony and the sheepdog bred there go by this pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name for a Shetland sheepdog or Shetland pony.

clue.text: Privileged bridge players with prospect of making it

parts.note: East and North are two partners at bridge, E and N
viable means capable of succeeding

explanation.surface: Bridge players who seem likely to make their contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Privileged and enviable both describe a position others would covet.

clue.text: Inspirer of festivities to sponsor our group, say

indicators.note: say tells us the letters are spoken and give a word of like sound

parts.note: to sponsor is to back; our group is us

explanation.surface: Someone who funds the party for our gang.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK US, said aloud, gives the name of the Roman god of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of wine, patron of revelry.

clue.text: Large-scale trading, involving thousands in 'railroad

indicators.note: involving says the force word wraps round the thousands

parts.note: to railroad someone is to coerce them
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so thousands is two Ms

explanation.surface: A big freight deal for railway shipments.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe before railroad is an OCR stray.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade conducted on a broad scale.

clue.text: Self-seekers say it's so, mistaken.

parts.note: say means for example, EG

indicators.note: mistaken says the letters of it's so are put wrong

explanation.surface: Selfish people insisting they are right while being wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: People concerned chiefly with themselves.

clue.text: Extent of greeting broadcast thereon?

parts.note: a wave is a greeting
extent means length

explanation.surface: Measuring how far a greeting reaches on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a radio programme goes out on a wavelength.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio signals travel on a particular frequency band.

clue.text: Popular church music

definitions.meaning: popular in the sense of for the many
a setting of the Eucharist liturgy to music

explanation.definitionFit: Mass market means popular; a Mass is a musical setting of the liturgy.

clue.text: Coach 'associated with scandal in …the theater

definitions.meaning: to coach is to train or teach

explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train them; Sheridan's comedy is The School for Scandal.

clue.text: Force to serve port

definitions.meaning: to kidnap someone into service as a sailor

explanation.definitionFit: To press-gang men aboard ship; also the Chinese seaport.

clue.text: Male on road, one employed as driver

parts.note: he refers to a male

explanation.surface: A man on the road working as a driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver drives cattle: a herd is an old word for a herdsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman, who drives livestock.

clue.text: Stuck-up head of religious order.

definitions.meaning: the head of a monastery or convent

explanation.definitionFit: A haughty air is lofty; the Mother or Father heading a convent holds this title.

clue.text: Cake made by girl moving back to front

indicators.note: moving back to front says the last letter is shifted to the start

parts.note: Claire is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl walking backwards with a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving back to front' takes the final E of CLAIRE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry filled with cream, a kind of cake.

clue.text: With tact, though in a detached manner, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says a word is chosen for how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: discretely means separately, as distinct parts

explanation.surface: Acting tactfully while seeming aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: The two spellings are said the same: the one with ET means separately, the one with EE tactfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactfully, with careful prudence.
